name: Microscope
description: A white compound microscope with three objectives on a turret, a square stage with slide clips, and a lamp in the base. The lamp needs power; daylight and a mirror will do.
notes: 340 mm tall on a base 140 by 190 mm: back pillar and arm, coarse and fine focus knobs, stage over a condenser, three steel objectives (one red-banded) and an upright eyepiece; enamel-white body, plastic-black stage. The tiles draw the slide and lamp lens opaque. magnifying and analysis are quality names already in use.

name: Dissecting microscope
description: A stereo microscope with two eyepieces on a pillar stand, for looking at the surface of small things in depth while working on them.
notes: 316 mm tall on a charcoal base 200 by 240 mm with a white stage plate and clips, a steel pillar, a focus block and a white head with zoom knobs and two eyepieces slanting toward the user. Less magnification than the compound microscope, so magnifying 2, above a magnifying glass.

name: Multimeter
description: A handheld digital meter in a yellow rubber holster, with a range dial and red and black probes. Measures voltage, current, resistance and continuity.
notes: 150 by 80 mm and 32 mm thick lying face up: lcd-green display, three keys, rotary dial, three sockets with two plugged leads running to probes laid along its side. electronics_testing is a new quality name for finding faults in circuits and wiring; the voltmeter shares it at a lower level.

name: Voltmeter
description: A bench meter with a needle dial and two binding posts, its red and black probes on short leads. Reads the voltage between two points.
notes: Case 130 wide, 110 tall and 90 deep with a white arc scale, black needle, zero screw and red and black posts; probes lie in front, making the box 240 mm deep. The dial has no glass so the needle reads in the tiles. electronics_testing at 1, below the multimeter's 2, because it only measures voltage.

name: Microcentrifuge
description: A benchtop centrifuge for small sample tubes: a round body with a clear lid window over the rotor and a small control panel. Needs power.
notes: 194 mm across, 124 mm tall and 238 mm deep with the sloped panel; plastic-white body, grey lid, plastic-clear window over a charcoal rotor, lcd-green display and two keys. The tiles draw the window opaque. centrifuging is a new quality name for separating samples by spinning them.

name: Melting point apparatus
description: A hot plate with a heated housing on top. A sample in a thin glass tube goes into a slot and is watched through a magnifier as it warms, to find the temperature it melts at and so tell what it is and how pure. Needs power.
notes: 200 mm square and 188 mm tall to the capillary tip: grey base with steel plate, lcd-green display and keys, charcoal housing with three slots, a magnifier viewport under a lamp hood, and a capillary in one slot. CHECK VOLUME (x5.1): the reference's 1.5 L is too small for a 5 kg bench instrument; the box follows a real unit's size. The tiles draw the lens and capillary opaque.

name: pH meter
description: A bench meter with two glass electrodes held over a beaker on a stand, and a bottle of buffer solution for setting it. Reads how acid or alkaline a liquid is.
notes: Case 160 by 140 mm with a sloped lcd-green display and three keys; a steel stand rod 220 mm tall with an arm holding two electrodes in a beaker of water; a frosted buffer bottle with a blue cap. CHECK VOLUME (x6.4): the reference's 1.5 L counts the meter packed away; set up on its stand it spans 232 by 188 mm and 220 mm tall. The tiles draw the beaker and electrodes opaque. The buffer is drawn as part of the kit, not a separate item.

name: Spectrophotometer
description: A benchtop instrument that shines light through a liquid sample in a small square cuvette and measures how much is absorbed, for telling what is in a solution and how much. Needs power.
notes: 300 wide, 130 tall and 230 deep: white case with a grey hinged sample lid and vent, a low front deck with a screen-black display and six keys, a plastic-clear cuvette of orange sample beside it. CHECK VOLUME (x4.8): the reference's 2 L is too small for a 5 kg bench instrument; the box follows a real unit's size.

name: Sextant
description: A navigator's sextant with a graduated arc, a swinging arm, two mirrors, shade glasses and a small telescope. Measures the sun's height above the horizon to find your latitude.
notes: Lying on its side, 246 by 224 mm and 46 mm thick: black plastic frame, white graduated arc with ticks, grey index arm with vernier, mirror-silver index and horizon mirrors, lens-smoke and green shade glasses, charcoal telescope and a handle underneath. Plastic as the reference has it. CHECK VOLUME (x5.1): the frame is open and the box counts the air inside it. navigation is a new quality name.

name: Ring stand clamps
description: A shallow open tray of mismatched clamps for a laboratory stand: a support ring, a three-prong clamp, spare boss heads and a loose wing nut. One jaw is held together with tape.
notes: Low tray 120 by 80 mm with 25 mm corrugated cardboard walls and a light paper-butcher floor so the contents show, holding a 70 mm steel support ring lying flat with its arm, a clamp rod, alu boss heads, red clamp jaws taped with tape-silver standing just above the rim, and a wing nut; 120 by 46 by 80 mm overall. A crafting part for building lab stands and glassware rigs, so it brings no quality of its own.

name: Makeshift nitrogen generator
description: A homemade rig on a steel skid that pulls nitrogen out of the air: an intake filter for dust, a column of drying salts for moisture, and a long membrane that separates the nitrogen, with a gauge and an outlet valve. Needs a supply of compressed air.
notes: 1.5 m long on an angle-steel skid 400 mm wide: black filter canister with pleated face, steel-bright drying column with a salt-white sight strip, white membrane module on two saddles, brass manifold with a gauge and red-handled valve, rubber-black hoses; 610 mm tall. CHECK VOLUME (x5.2): the skid is open and the box counts the air round the parts. A placed machine rather than a carried item; the size is only a placeholder. nitrogen_supply is a new quality name.

name: Rotary evaporator
description: A motor turns a round flask half sunk in a heated water bath, boiling its contents off gently; the vapour climbs to a coiled glass condenser and drips into a second flask. Strips solvents and concentrates extracts. Needs power.
notes: 648 wide, 680 tall and 364 deep: grey base with a bath display, steel-stainless bath of water, grey tower with a motor head and speed knob, a glass vapour duct slanting down to the rotating flask, a glass condenser with a frosted coil and hose barbs, and a receiving flask; both flasks hold syrup-orange liquid. The tiles draw glass and water opaque. A placed bench machine; the size is only a placeholder. distilling is a quality name already in use.

name: Teleport pad
description: A flat aluminium plate with a ring of copper emitter coils round a glowing core and a small solar cell in one corner. Laid on the ground, it throws whoever steps on it somewhere else.
notes: 300 mm square and 28 mm thick: alu-bare plate with a charcoal rim, copper coil ring, six emitter nodes, crystal-glow-blue core, a screen-black solar cell and a trigger plate. Setting it as a trap needs a placed-trap field the item schema does not have yet, so it brings no quality.

name: Teleporter
description: An experimental handheld device: a pistol grip under an aluminium barrel wound with copper coils round a glowing core, with a forked emitter at the front. Pressing the button throws you a short distance in some direction.
notes: 236 mm long and 134 mm tall, emitter at +x: matte black grip and end cap, alu-bare barrel, five copper coils over a crystal-glow-blue core, forked emitter with glowing tips and a red button. The reference counts it in stacks of 20 with 1.36 kg each; a stack of devices makes no sense, so it is one item at 1.36 kg. Its use needs an activation action the item schema does not have yet, so it brings no quality.

name: Vacuum pump
description: A heavy belt-driven pump on a steel base, with its motor alongside and an oil sight glass on the front. Draws a deep vacuum for lab glassware, refrigeration work and degassing. Needs power.
notes: 480 long, 304 tall and 236 deep: paint-green motor with a parkerized fan cover, a steel-grey pump block with an amber oil sight glass, brass inlet port, exhaust and oil cap, a green belt guard along the back and a carry handle. CHECK VOLUME (x5.7): the reference's 6 L is too small for a 22.7 kg pump; the box follows a real unit's size. Iron per the reference; painted cast iron reads too dark, so the block uses steel-grey. vacuum is a new quality name.
